info.name: LedgerOne - Accounting (Journal Entries)
info.description:
Journal Entries submodule API collection (Create, Get, List, Update, Submit, Reject, Post, Reverse). Reflects the implementation exactly as shipped in apps/api/src/shared/accounting. Does not modify or duplicate FinancialYear/FiscalPeriod/ChartOfAccounts.postman_collection.json — this collection creates its own Account Group/Account/Financial Year/Fiscal Period fixtures as setup steps.

Design note (JWT required): same convention as every other collection in this folder — every protected request carries `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`, the same long-lived (10-year) RS256 dev-only token for tenantId 900001 already used by FinancialYear/FiscalPeriod/ChartOfAccounts/Currency/Tax.

Design note (no X-Tenant-Id validation-failure case): identical reasoning to every other collection here — current-tenant.middleware.ts derives `req.tenantId` from the verified JWT claim and overwrites `X-Tenant-Id` in place server-side, so this collection's `X-Tenant-Id: {{tenantId}}` header is inert structural consistency, not a real validation path.

Design note (Ledger has no endpoints): 00_BUSINESS_RULES.md Ch.19.18 — 'Only the Journal Entry posting process may create Ledger entries — no direct, manual creation or editing... is permitted through any interface.' This collection therefore never calls a `/ledger-*` path (none exists); Ledger Entry creation is verified indirectly, by inspecting the database directly outside Postman (see the milestone's own verification notes), not asserted here.

Design note (two Financial Year/Fiscal Period fixture families): the primary fixture (`{{jeYear}}`, a random far-future year, base 6000, distinct from every other collection's own base/modulus so runs never collide) is used for ordinary Create/Get/List/Update/Submit/Reject/Post/first-half testing. A SECOND fixture family covers the REAL current date (computed once per run from `new Date()`) because `reverseJournalEntry`'s reversing entry always posts at 'now' (domain/interfaces/clock.interface.ts's own documented decision) — reversal would otherwise fail with ACC_NO_FISCAL_PERIOD_FOR_POSTING_DATE against a fixture dated centuries in the future. TWO MORE fixture families (`{{closedFyYear}}`, `{{closedFpYear}}`) exist purely to construct a Closed Financial Year and a Closed Fiscal Period respectively, for the two 403 tests that need them.

Design note (balance NOT checked at creation): create-journal-entry.service.ts deliberately defers DBL-001 balance checking to posting time (Ch.16.6's workflow diagram gates POSTING, not Draft creation) — 'Create Journal Entry - Success (Unbalanced, Allowed As Draft)' below is not a bug demonstration, it is asserting this documented, intentional behavior; the corresponding rejection is exercised at posting time instead ('Post Journal Entry - Unbalanced (422)').

Design note (`.min(2)` at the DTO layer): create-journal-entry.dto.ts's Zod schema already rejects a `lines` array shorter than 2 before the request ever reaches the Business layer — 'Create Journal Entry - Validation Error (Fewer Than Two Lines)' below therefore returns `VALIDATION_ERROR` (Zod), not `ACC_JOURNAL_ENTRY_MINIMUM_LINES` (the deeper Business-layer error, which exists as defense-in-depth for any future direct Business-layer caller and is exercised by this module's own Jest unit tests, not reachable through this HTTP boundary).

Known gap: List is unpaginated, same flagged Repository-layer limitation as every other list endpoint in this module. A second known gap, discovered while building this collection: `reverseJournalEntry` is not fully transactional end-to-end (create-reversal, post-reversal, mark-original-reversed are three sequential Business-layer calls) — if the post step fails (e.g. no covering Open Fiscal Period for 'now'), the freshly-created reversing Journal Entry is left behind in Draft status, orphaned. Both gaps are pre-existing, documented Business-layer milestone risks, not introduced by this collection.

Run order for a full pass, top to bottom: every 'Setup' request must run first, in order, to seed fixture variables; every non-setup request chains off the uuids those setup requests save.

item.name: Create Financial Year (Current, Setup — for Reversal)

request.description: Covers the REAL current date, since reverseJournalEntry always posts the reversing entry at 'now' — unlike every other fixture in this collection, this one is NOT randomized (it cannot be; it must contain today), so re-running this collection on the same calendar day would otherwise collide with the previous run's leftover row (FinancialYearOverlapError). The test script below makes this step idempotent: on 409, it looks up and reuses the already-existing Financial Year instead of failing, so the collection is safely re-runnable without manual cleanup between runs.
